correctness.rationale: For any support of size at least three, shattering iff each element is a strict coordinate minimum or maximum among support points: necessity via excluding one point from a box containing all others; sufficiency by bounding boxes for nonempty labels and a singleton outside the support, guaranteed by N>=K+1. Each coordinate has at most two extrema, but binary coordinates only one. For m>=3, single specified minimum/maximum events each have L_m(n) assignments; a pair of different specified points can have both extrema only in opposite orientations, with E_m(n) choices each. Three intersections are impossible, so two-level inclusion–exclusion yields exactly the coefficient formula. For maximal support size K, role bijections give the leading coefficient factorization. Singleton and two-point boundary cases are separately proved. A direct trace enumerator tested 48,917 supports exhaustively on fourteen grids and 28,500 additional supports on three larger grids; tests corroborate but do not replace the general proof.

originality.rationale: An accessible prior two-dimensional Cartesian path-grid census gives the complete shattering polynomial for the same interval-box geometry (plus an empty hypothesis), so the planar formula and private-extreme criterion are explicitly credited and not claimed new. The present theorem concerns arbitrary products of finite chains: unbounded VC degree, all coefficient formulas for every d, and the highest-degree factorization. The planar formula by itself does not determine higher-dimensional coefficients; nor do arXiv:2004.13861 (periodic torus dimension) or arXiv:1511.08245 (abstract Hilbert bounds). Extensive alternative-terminology search located no dominating arbitrary-dimensional enumeration. Best-knowledge priority remains qualified.

value.rationale: The result determines a complete structural classification and every support-count coefficient of a natural finite definable range space on arbitrary products of chains. This is not only the standard continuous VC dimension: the binary-versus-ternary threshold changes the dimension, and two equal-dimension grids (ternary square versus four-dimensional Boolean cube) have different shattering polynomials. The exact coefficient formula gives uniform-random-support probabilities, while the largest-degree coefficient has a simple product form not apparent from a dimension bound. Arbitrarily unequal alphabet lengths and tied coordinates are covered.
